definition: A patch lies closer to A when light-toned, relatively uniform surfaces dominate, such as snow or exposed agricultural ground, often with bright red crop parcels in false color. It lies closer to B when dark water or rugged land with extensive dark slopes and shadows dominates. Judge the overall area and brightness of these surfaces.
cues: Large expanses of white or pale ground favor A; extensive deep blue, brown-black or black surfaces favor B.
Broad, bright red agricultural parcels in false color favor A; predominantly dark or muted false color favors B.
Regular field strips or continuous snow cover favor A.
Strongly shaded ridges and valleys, or dark water with fine ripple texture, favor B.
